parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the inverted image produced by a converging lens. Refer to Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Measure the height h O of the triangular object provided. h O = ........................................................... cm • Place the lens a distance u = 20.0 cm from the illuminated triangular object. • Place the screen close to the lens. • Switch on the lamp. • Move the screen away from the lens until a clear focused image of the triangular object is seen on the screen. • Measure, and record in Table 3.1, the height h I of the image. Describe one technique you used to produce an image on the screen which is as sharp as possible in this experiment. ........................................................................................................................................... ........................................................................................................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(i)
ms.text:
sensible value for hO (1.5 to 2.5 (cm)) present and
suitable technique for focus e.g.
move screen slowly / back and forth

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Repeat the procedure for u = 25.0 cm, u = 30.0 cm, u = 35.0 cm and u = 40.0 cm. Switch off the lamp. Table 3.1 u / cm h I / cm D / 1 cm 20.0 25.0 30.0 35.0 40.0 [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) For each distance u, calculate, and record in Table 3.1, a value D. Use your values of h I from Table 3.1 and the equation: D = 1 h I . [1]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text: D calculations correct, and at least 2 significant figures

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of u / cm (y-axis) against D / 1 cm (x-axis). Start the axes at the origin (0,0). Draw a best-fit straight line. [4]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
graph:
•
axes correct way round and labelled with quantity and unit
•
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
•
plots all correct to ½ small square, precise plots
•
well judged line and thin line

parts.label: i
parts.text: (d) (i) From your graph, determine u 0 , the value of u when D is zero. u 0 = ..................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = .......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(d)(ii)
ms.text: G recorded and triangle method shown on graph

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the focal length f of the lens. Use your value of h O from (a) and the equation: f = G h O × k, where k = 1.0 cm 2 . f = ..................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
any appropriate difficulty:
e.g. hand / ruler in way of image / person creating a shadow
and matching improvement:
e.g. use translucent screen and view from behind /
fix ruler or grid to screen / mark image on screen before measuring / take a photo with ruler in view
